title.narrative: Establishing Temporary Learning Spaces for Conflict-Affected School-Aged Children in Gaza, Featuring the Procurement and Installation of Tents in both UNRWA DESs and Makeshift Sites

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian crisis in Gaza has escalated into a catastrophic emergency. Over the past year, ongoing conflict has forced nearly 1.9 million people to flee their homes, leading to widespread destruction of housing and essential services. This dire situation severely restricts families' access to basic needs, especially education.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAs hostilities intensified, countless families sought refuge in UNRWA emergency shelters, primarily located within school buildings. The disruption of formal education has caused lasting damage to children’s learning, exposing them to ongoing trauma anxiety. In response, UNRWA has provided Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), deploying trained counselors to offer vital emotional support alleviate distress among affected children. Additionally, UNRWA has adopted a non-formal education strategy, utilizing innovative radio programs to keep children engaged in learning.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOn August 1, 2024, UNRWA launched the “Back to Learning” initiative, establishing temporary learning spaces in 45 locations by September 14, encouraging children to regain a sense of normalcy. This strategy fosters resilience equips children with vital coping mechanisms to navigate their challenging circumstances.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe damage to educational facilities is staggering since the conflict began on October 7, 2023, around 85% of schools in Gaza have been affected. Many UNRWA schools, once safe havens, have become overcrowded shelters for displaced families. With nearly 70% of schools inoperable, the need for alternative learning spaces has reached critical levels.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo expand access to education, this project proposes the procurement installation of 129 tents to create Temporary Learning Spaces (TLS). Of these, 105 tents will be strategically placed within UNRWA-designated emergency shelters (DES), selected based on the highest concentrations of displaced families and children in North Gaza, Gaza City, North Middle, South Middle, and Khan Younis. Additionally, 24 tents will be set up in makeshift sites in the Middle and Khan Younis-Mawasi areas.ltbrgtThis proposal outlines two types of tent classroom installations: one in UNRWA DESs and another in makeshift sites.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtTLS Tents in UNRWA DES:lt/bgt These classrooms will feature a closed shading shed design measuring 7.5x6 meters, built from agricultural steel. Key features include six reinforced columns, a weather-resistant tarpaulin cover, and a complete electrical system for lighting and ventilation. The installation ensures stability and safety through concrete foundations and flooring.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtTLS Tents in Makeshift Sites:lt/bgt While similar in design and size, these classrooms will lack electrical connections. They will focus on maintaining a functional learning environment with structural stability through concrete beams and a tarpaulin cover but will not include electrical features.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThese TLS tents will serve as versatile spaces—facilitating educational activities while also functioning as venues for MHPSS when not in use for learning. This dual-purpose approach maximizes resources for children and families, enhancing their social and emotional well-being. By aligning this initiative with UNRWA’s ongoing support for unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), we aim to address the diverse needs of vulnerable children.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltugtIn Gaza and the North areas, the education cluster acknowledges that UNRWA has not yet started its non-formal activities. This delay is due to essential tasks that UNMAS must complete first. UNRWA cannot begin operations until TLS sites are fully cleared. The Education Program has identified these sites and assigned staff, ready to start once UNMAS grants clearance.lt/ugtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough these non-formal learning opportunities, we empower conflict-affected school-aged children to reclaim their right to education, fostering growth, resilience, and hope. This project stands as a beacon of hope, striving to restore normalcy and nurture the future of Gaza’s children amidst the shadows of conflict.ltbrgtlt/pgt
